gate.mark_plan:
PLAN GATE: `{name}` is PENDING: a required check did not pass.
Fix the findings IN THE PLAN and save it again: the plan is approved automatically when every required check passes. To run the checks now:
  {gate} run-checks {path}
`release` is a human decision, not a way out: run it only when the person who decides tells you to, with their reason:
  {gate} release {path} --reason "<what was decided>"
Implementation is blocked until then.
gate.mark_spec:
SPEC GATE: `{name}` is PENDING: a required check did not pass.
Fix the findings IN THE SPEC and save it again: the spec is approved automatically when every required check passes. To see the findings and run the checks now:
  {spec_preflight} {path}
  {gate} run-checks {path}
`release` is a human decision, not a way out: run it only when the person who decides tells you to, with their reason:
  {gate} release {path} --reason "<what was decided>"
⚠️ A spec error passes by construction in the plan review: it checks the plan AGAINST the spec, so the two agree.
gate.deny_spec:
BLOCKED BY THE SPEC GATE.

Spec(s) without approval or release: {names}

A plan does not start with a pending spec. Do ONE of these:
  1. Fix the findings IN THE SPEC and save it. The spec is approved automatically when every required check passes:
     {spec_preflight} <spec>
     {gate} run-checks <spec>
  2. `release` is a human decision: only when the person who decides says to go on as is, with their reason:
     {gate} release <spec> --reason "<what was decided>"

⚠️ The plan review checks the plan AGAINST the spec. If the spec lies,
the two agree and pass -- no review downstream catches it.
gate.deny_plan:
BLOCKED BY THE PLAN GATE.

Plan(s) without approval or release: {names}

Implementation does not start with a pending plan. Do ONE of these:
  1. Fix the findings IN THE PLAN and save it. The plan is approved automatically when every required check passes:
     {gate} run-checks <plan>
  2. `release` is a human decision: only when the person who decides says to go on as is, with their reason:
     {gate} release <plan> --reason "<what was decided>"

⚠️ The preflight is `grep`: it is NOT an adversarial review. It finds what is mechanical,
and what is left -- composition between tasks, reuse gate, a defense that does not reach the
exit path -- stays with you.
⚠️ Do not get around the gate by another path (another tool, another shell).
Getting around it instead of solving it is the defect it exists to catch.

gate.changed_after_release: the plan changed after the release

gate.false_positive_wrong_state: NOT RELEASED: --false-positive is for a group with findings; `{group}` is {state}. For a check that did not run use --no-coverage.
gate.spec_false_positive_wrong_state: NOT RELEASED: --false-positive is for a blocking spec group with findings; `{group}` is {state}.

    fix it in the PLAN, or escape with {verb} {group}="<why>"
gate.changed_during_check: NOT RELEASED: the plan changed during the check. Run it again.

gate.help:
plan_gate.py — plan-first gate

  status [plan]                 shows the state of the plans of this repo
  release <plan> --reason R     human override, with a trail (--false-positive G=…, --no-coverage G=…, --despite-check ID=…)
  run-checks <path>             runs the registered checks; approves when every required one passes
  hash <file>                   prints the content hash the gate records
  config <path>                 prints the resolved repo config as JSON
  checks list|prune             lists the registered checks / removes the orphans

Hook subcommands: mark, check, register-check <manifest>, register-checks.
gate.config_unreadable: the repo config cannot be used: {error}
gate.manual_error:
ERROR in `{sub}`: {error}
Nothing was written. Details in {log}
search.positive_glob: POSITIVE glob in `find` is not supported: the two engines diverge in depth. Use `list_files`, which has its own path for that.
preflight.alias_missing: alias `{alias}` used {n}x in the plan and MISSING from: {missing}. The import does not resolve.
preflight.symbol_order: `{name}()` is created in Task {created} but consumed in Task {used}. The intermediate task goes red (rule 20).
preflight.symbol_invented: `{name}()` (Task {task}) does NOT exist in the repo and NO task creates it. Invented method (rule 14).
preflight.constant_decorative: constant `{name}` (Task {task}) appears {uses}x in the plan — defined and never consumed. Decorative constraint (rule 17b).
preflight.fo.nullish_list: `?? []` — absence turning into an empty list
preflight.fo.or_list: `|| []` — absence turning into an empty list
preflight.fo.nullish_object: `?? {}` — absence turning into an empty object
preflight.fo.catch_empty_list: catch writing an empty list — error read as 'there is no data'
preflight.fo.substring_status: HTTP status by substring of the message
preflight.modify_missing: `Modify: {target}` — file not found in this repo or its sibling repos. Wrong path, or should it be Create?
preflight.not_committed: `{target}` (Task {task}) is created but does NOT appear in any `git add` of the plan.
preflight.coverage_tsc: Task {task}: creates `{file}`, and the task's `tsc --noEmit` filter (`{filters}`) does not reach it. A type error in it would not show up — and vitest does NOT type-check, it runs on esbuild.
preflight.coverage_none: Task {task}: creates `{file}`, but no verification command of the task reaches it (filters: `{filters}`). The step goes green without having looked at it.
preflight.not_a_list: the check returned {type}, not a list
preflight.plan_not_utf8: the plan is not valid UTF-8 (byte {byte}); cannot check what cannot be read
preflight.reason_no_task: no task recognized in the plan (I look for `## Task N:` or `### Task N:`)
preflight.reason_alias_broken: there is an alias configuration in the repo and it does not parse
preflight.reason_no_alias: the repo does not declare import aliases
preflight.reason_fences: there are {fences} fence(s) and only {blocks} readable block(s)
preflight.reason_language: there is a code block, none in a language in the table ({languages})
preflight.reason_no_code_block: the plan has no code block
preflight.reason_constant_language: there is a code block in a language outside the table: I do not know how to recognize a constant declaration
preflight.reason_no_constant: the plan does not declare an UPPER_SNAKE constant
preflight.reason_files_unrecognized: there is a **Files:** section and no `- Create|Modify|Test:` line was recognized
preflight.reason_no_verifiable_item: there are tasks and none creates a verifiable item
preflight.group.created-not-committed: File created that does not enter a commit
preflight.group.verification-gap: Verification that does not cover what the task creates
preflight.not_ok: Not OK — it is the absence of a check.
preflight.summary_not_run: ⚠️ {n} check(s) DID NOT RUN. This is not 'ok': it is the absence of a check.
preflight.summary_findings: ⚠️ {n} MECHANICAL finding(s). Fix them BEFORE releasing the plan.
preflight.summary_clean_1: Nothing mechanical pending. What is left is what grep does not see: composition between
preflight.summary_clean_2: tasks, reuse gate, a defense that does not reach the output path, and a test that does not
preflight.nothing_to_check: no group had anything to check (the plan has no code block, Files section or verifiable item): a pass here would be vacuous
preflight.orphans_none:
### Check 7 -- field/symbol declared and not propagated

No orphan: the {n} fields declared in code blocks appear in more than one place of the plan.
preflight.orphans_found:
### Check 7 -- field/symbol declared and NOT propagated

**{n} symbol(s) appear ONCE in the plan: only in the declaration.**
An options/type field that nobody reads was the defect that cost 3 blocks on
17/09 (`email`, `somentePrioritarios`, `destacaPrioritarios`): the plan
explained in a comment what should happen, without the line that does it.

{items}

⚠️ Check that the plan shows **who READS** each one. A field that crosses a
chain (`execute` -> `rodar` -> `executarCanal`) has to appear in EVERY link;
a single citation means that no link receives it.
preflight.c6_missing: **Cited and NOT found in the repo:** {items}
preflight.c6_missing_note: (Same as the table above: if the plan PROMISES to create them, that is expected -- check the order of the tasks. A runtime/deploy path also falls here.)
preflight.c6_approx_head: **Matched by NAME, not by path** -- the exact path cited does NOT exist today; the content below is from the homonymous file that exists:
preflight.c6_approx_note: (If the plan MOVES or CREATES the file at the cited path, this is expected. If it READS from the cited path, the path is what is wrong.)
preflight.c6_injected_1: **Full content below, with line numbers.** These files are already
preflight.c6_injected_2: in your context: do NOT spend a call rereading with `nl`/`sed`/`cat`.
preflight.c6_injected_3: Cite them as evidence in the `file:line` format.
preflight.c6_on_demand: **They exist, but are NOT in your context** (cited fewer than {minimum}x, or too big) -- read on demand, only the slice you need:
preflight.p_title: ## Mechanical preflight -- ALREADY RUN locally. Do NOT redo these greps.
preflight.p_searched: Searched in `{repo_name}` with {engine}, excluding `{excluded}/`. This answers checks 1, 5 and 6.
preflight.p_missing:
**DO NOT EXIST in the repo — zero definitions, zero uses ({n}).**
These are the symbols the plan CREATES in a task, or invokes without ever creating.
`plan:N` = line of the PLAN where it is invoked (no need to grep):
preflight.p_outside: **Used in the repo but defined outside it** (framework/vendor) -- nothing to check here:
preflight.p_constants_header: | constant | definition found | uses in the repo | citations in the plan |
preflight.p_how_title: ### How to read this preflight -- read before opening a finding
preflight.p_how_1:
⚠️ **DOES NOT EXIST is not, by itself, a block.** Almost every new symbol the
plan creates shows up here, and that is expected. What you check is the ORDER:
is there a task that CREATES it **before** the task that consumes it? If the plan invokes
the symbol and no task creates it, then it is a BLOCK (check 1).
preflight.p_how_2:
⚠️ Decorative constant (check 5) = **uses in the repo 0 AND citations in the plan 1**
-- defined and never consumed. Two or more citations already indicate consumption; read
where, because the count does not tell a definition from a use.
preflight.p_how_3:
⚠️ The search EXCLUDED `docs/`, so the plan itself never counts as a use. A
symbol with uses > 0 is really in code.
preflight.p_ran_full:
⚠️ These greps were already run and the files above are already in your context:
cite them as evidence instead of spending a call repeating the read.
preflight.p_ran_incremental:
⚠️ These greps were already run:
cite them as evidence instead of spending a call repeating the read.
preflight.p_how_4:
Save your calls for what the preflight does NOT answer: permission gates,
order between tasks, side effects, type contracts, git history.
preflight.cli_description: Mechanical preflight of an implementation plan
preflight.cli_epilog: Exit codes: 0 = nothing mechanical pending; 1 = there is a finding; 2 = some check came out NOT EVALUATED (did not run). 2 is never 'ok': it is the absence of a check.
preflight.cli_prompt: block of greps for the reviewer prompt
preflight.cli_json: machine-readable check: {status, findings[{group,state,count,items}]}; same exit codes
preflight.cli_promises: noisy advisory; NEVER changes the exit code
preflight.not_in_repo: the plan must be inside a git repo
preflight.promises_head: [ -- ] Spec promises (advisory, does NOT count for the gate)
spec.group.support: Citation that does not support the sentence
spec.group.claims: Claim about the repo without a citation
spec.blocked_1: ⚠️ There is a GUARANTEE claim without proof, a broken citation or a nonexistent
spec.blocked_2: symbol. Cite `file:line` checked NOW, or write
spec.blocked_3: NOT VERIFIED. A claim from memory is the defect this catches.
spec.clean: No blocking finding. The warnings above are still yours.
spec.citation_outside: `{arq}:{lin}` — outside this repo; I cannot check it
spec.citation_past_end: `{arq}:{lin}` — the file has {total} lines; the citation points outside it
spec.citation_unsupported: `{arq}:{lin}` does not mention {absent} (±{window} lines) — the citation does not support the sentence
spec.nothing_to_check: the spec has no citation and no claim the checks could examine: a pass here would be vacuous
gate.checks_failed: Registered checks that did not pass:
gate.despite_unknown_check: --despite-check {check} is not a required check here (required: {checks}).
gate.despite_check_passed: --despite-check `{check}`: that check PASSES -- there is nothing to release despite.
gate.despite_check_hint: Fix what the check reports, or -- only when the person who decides says so -- add --despite-check {check}="<why>".
gate.orphan_checks:
⚠️ Orphan check(s) -- their command no longer exists, and they block until removed: {ids}
   {gate} checks prune
gate.corrupted_checks:
⚠️ Corrupted check manifest(s) -- they count as required checks that fail: {ids}
   Fix or remove the file(s) in {folder} (`checks prune` does not remove them).
gate.not_gated: not a plan or a spec: {path}
gate.no_required_checks: no required check applies -- nothing is approved automatically; release with --reason
checks.not_an_object: a check must be an object, not {got}
checks.bad_id: invalid check id {got} (letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'; no leading dot)
checks.reserved_id: check id {got} is reserved: ids starting with 'inbox-' name the gate's own inbox error records
checks.bad_command: check {id}: `command` must be a non-empty string
checks.id_mismatch: the id {id} does not match the file name {file}
checks.orphan: check {id} is orphan: {paths} does not exist -- run `{gate} checks prune`
checks.unparsable: check {id}: the command cannot be split into arguments ({error})
checks.timed_out: check {id} did not finish within {timeout} s
checks.bad_output: check {id} did not print the contract JSON {{"status": "pass"|"fail", "findings": [...]}} (exit {rc}; stdout: {stdout!r}; stderr: {stderr!r})
checks.inbox_bad_entry: the inbox entry needs absolute "manifest" and "plugin_root"
checks.inbox_failed: plugin `{plugin}` announced a check the gate could not register ({error}; entry {source}). Reinstall the plugin, or remove it and run `checks prune`.
checks.corrupted_kept: corrupted manifest(s) not removed: {ids} -- prune removes orphans only; fix or delete them in {folder}
checks.duplicate_in_manifest: the id {id} appears more than once in the manifest -- nothing registered
checks.conflict: ⚠️ check {id} is registered by more than one manifest ({sources}): kept as a conflict, which fails until one is removed
checks.conflict_entry: check {id} is claimed by more than one manifest: {sources} -- remove the duplicate and delete this file
checks.not_registered: check {id} is required by the repo config (.claude/plan-gate.json) but not registered
checks.pass_with_failing_exit: check {id} printed "pass" but exited {rc} -- an incoherent pass is not a pass
gate.missing_checks: ⚠️ Check(s) required by .claude/plan-gate.json but not registered -- they block until registered or made optional: {ids}
checks.left_corrupted: check {id} not registered: {file} is corrupted and counts as a failing required check -- fix or delete it
gate.two_gates: Both gates are blocking: the INTERNAL plugin `revisao-de-plano@pentagrama` is enabled in {settings}. Each gate keeps its own state, so you would have to release every plan twice. To switch the old one off, set `"PORTAO_DE_PLANO": "off"` in the `env` block of ~/.claude/settings.json.
phase.usage: usage: phase.py start [#N] [--branch B] | phase.py <name> | phase.py report
phase.bad_name: `{name}` is not a valid phase name: use lowercase letters and `_` (`review`, `validation`, `delivered`); `start` goes through `phase.py start`.
phase.bad_issue: `{value}` is not an issue number: use `phase.py start 58` or `phase.py start #58`.
phase.no_repo: Not inside a git repository: nothing was stamped.
delivery.not_run_none: **Not run:** nothing -- every verification listed above ran.
delivery.no_closes: Warning: no `Closes #N` line -- the target is not the default branch (or the default branch or the issue is unknown). Link the issue in the description; it will have to be closed by hand after the merge.
delivery.outcome.error: Failed before or without a usable answer; see `error`. Nothing to retry blindly.
delivery.outcome.refused: The platform refused the request (4xx); fix the cause before trying again.
delivery.outcome.retryable: Rate limited (429); wait and try again.
delivery.outcome.unknown: The request was sent and no clear answer came back: it MAY exist. Before any retry, look it up: `open-request --branch <branch>` for an MR/PR, `notes --issue <N>` for an issue comment, `verify` for a description update.
gate.deny_state_dir:
BLOCKED BY THE PLAN GATE: {path} is inside the gate's state folder ({folder}).
Nothing legitimate writes there through a tool: a plan is approved by its checks and released by a human. Writing the state or a check manifest by hand is self-approval.
gate.deny_review_state:
BLOCKED BY THE PLAN GATE: {path} is inside a review state folder (~/.claude/claude-workflow/, PLAN_GATE_DIR or ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_DIR) while a plan or spec is pending.
A verdict is written by the review itself (review.py), never by hand: writing one is self-approval. Run the review, or ask the person who decides.
gate.corrupt_state: ⚠️ Unreadable gate state {file} ({error}): it counts as PENDING for {target}. Saving that file again rewrites the state.
gate.corrupt_state_unknown: ⚠️ Unreadable gate state {file} ({error}), of a file this gate cannot identify: it counts as pending and blocks implementation until a human checks it and removes it.
gate.no_coverage_not_for_spec: NOT RELEASED: --no-coverage is not accepted for a spec. It exists only for a plan group that did not run; for a spec finding you consider false use --false-positive on a blocking group.
gate.state_not_blocking: {state}, and it does not block a spec release
phase.bad_branch: `{value}` is not a valid branch name for `--branch`.
phase.reserved_name: `{name}` is stamped by the hooks or the gate, never by hand: a hand-made one would forge that boundary.
phase.config_warning: ⚠️ .claude/plan-gate.json cannot be read ({reason}); the stamp was written, the messages use the fallback language.
